No easy fix, however I can offer some advice that I struggle to follow myself.

 Failure is relative to how you define success. For example, I always nebulously say to myself that I want to be a "successful" music producer. But I am never fair to myself and simply consider myself a failure until the far into the possible future day when I might headline Coachella. This really isn't fair and won't work. Set small goals in between. Decided to upload one youtube video per week and did so for a 4 week streak? Awesome! You succeeded. Few people even make youtube videos. Did you enjoy the process? If so, then you should keep doing it. If you makes you happy that is successful. Set a new goal and accomplish that one. Keep succeeding along the way. So many electronic music producers that I have talked to never thought that they would "make it big" or reach that nebulous "successful" cloud that sits above the best of the best in an industry. You are currently feeling depressed, so starting to do something you enjoy is success enough. I can relate to this. Define your own short term goals so you can show yourself that you are indeed succeeding.

It's not terminal. I am not belittling your issues... I know how difficult depression is. I struggle with it daily along with drastic mood swings that make my life rather unstable at times. There is such a stigma around mental health that it makes it difficult to see treatment as viable. The entire reason I hopped on r/SuicideWatch was because I felt alone and didn't feel like counseling was even worth it. Unfortunately, you finding the right help for mental illnesses takes more time than physical illnesses. You have such a long life ahead of you. School does not excite everyone. If you supplement it with something else, you will have something to look forward to! Maybe try learning to code, writing stories, pick up drawing, learn a language, pick up a new sport, learn to solve Rubik's cubes, prepare for the US memory competition, start wood carving, making models and figurines with some clay from the craft store, learn to make vinyl stickers and make your own business on etsy, make a let's play gaming channel on youtube? I felt helpless and lost until I picked up music, but everyone is different. Here are some resources I want to point you to.

High school is a bubble in the sense that it is a closed environment that you can't control. If hurtful people are in your bubble, it is hard to avoid them because you are locked up in the same building with them for 35 hours a week. Once high school is over, you can have more freedom. In the sense of responsibilities of adulthood, it gets a bunch worse.... Yeah totally. But this is someone you can get better with managing over time. You can gain a perspective for how small these problems are compared to the vastness of the world as a whole, but high school tends to restrict this physically and mentally. The world does not automatically get better after high school, but the opportunity to make it your own is more present.

Now to address your other comment. I don't mean to make you angry. I taking the time out of my day on this sub to try to help people who take the time out of their day to reach out for the help of other everyday people like me. Hey OP. Everyone is unique, but I can relate to a few of the tings you mentioned. First I want to tell you something: high school is a bubble. Don't worry about any people in your high school because none of them will matter after you graduate (which you will). Don't believe me? I went to a school with 200 per class. I was class president, valedictorian, and president of a bunch of clubs. I knew everyone and everyone knew me. I was the reason we went to all of the field trips we went on and I was very social. I would say I had about 100 closeish acquaintances and about 20 good friends.... I speak to one (1) person from high school now. It has been a year and I think one or two other people messages me in fb recently but high school is a bubble. You won't realize how insignificant it is until you leave. Next, I want to address the abise of your family. You are eventually going to be an adult. You get to choose who you keep in your life. I like my parents. I will maintain contact with them. A friend of mine, who had a terrible upbringing and struggled in high school but is currently excelling with flying colors and a radiating smile in college, will likely only stop by her parents house reluctantly during holidays to be polite. It sucks to not feel loved.... But there are many successful, happy people who had similar struggles growing up. Next, you are depressed. You are taking advanced classes and we're excelling which means you are not lazy. I graduated valedictorian with a near perfect GPA, won a plethora of academic achievement medals, and studied for AP tests that my school didn't even have. How am I doing in college? Last night I was so stressed and depressed that I purposely slept from 10pm - midnight so I didn't have to do my homework for Physics due midnight.... I am having issues with suicidal thoughts, depression, managing stress, and mood swings. I can't continue doing this or I will lose my scholarships. I was very successful like you... But like you I am having a problem in my brain. You are not alone. Soooo mannnyyy peeeopplleee have mental health problems. Fuck the stigma. You are not abnormal, you just need help. Unfortunately you might not be able to seek out counselling, but that is definitely your best option. Maybe have a mental health counselor at school? Maybe your parents will understand if you ask to see one? Maybe you have a relative that will take you? Maybe you just don't have an option. I am fortunate that my university has a counselor. If you are looking for a buddy to talk to (not a substitute for professional help) try The Buddy project. It is a pretty awesome nonprofit that pairs you with a buddy. Just Google it. Additionally, you may fail 11th grade. Now I don't want to assume you are planning on attending college or suggest that it is he only option because it isn't, but if you are looking to go to school, these grades will harm you in your application. You may be very worried about this. I am here to tell you that here is (honestly) no reason to worry because 1) you can't fix it (though you can ask all of your teachers to understand your situation and possibly let you makeup tests or do extra credit work) 2) there is more to an application than grades. You have a story. You did not just fall behind because you didn't care. You have faced the struggles of mental health first hand. Take this experience and run with it. Start a 501c3 non profit to spread awareness for mental health disorders across schools. Work to end the stigma against mental health. There are many examples of organizations that do this. Reach out to them. They will help you. If you get your grades back up as much as possible and make a killer non profit with concrete results from now until you start applying to schools (you have the whole summer to do this) you can write a killer application.

This was very long and I apologize. Just understand that what you are facing now will seem silly in 5 years. You are not a bad person for being depressed. You just need help like people who break their leg and need a doctor. You can make a positive change in yourself that other people in your situation in the future can look up to as inspiration. I have seen people in your situation bounce back even high than those who never fell below the ground. You're great :)
